title: GKIDS Releases cocoon Wartime Anime Digitally With Blu-ray Disc Release Shipping on January 19
content:
GKIDS announced on Tuesday that it has released cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood ( cocoon Aru Natsu no Shōjo-tachi Yori ), the anime of Machiko Kyō 's Cocoon manga, digitally on Apple TV and Prime Video. The company will release the anime on Blu-ray Disc on January 19.

This year's JAPAN CUTS event screened the anime's North American premiere on July 10. The 30th annual Fantasia International Film Festival is screening the Canadian premiere.

The anime debuted on BS- NHK in March 2025, before airing on NHK General that August.

The anime stars Hikari Mitsushima as Mayu and Marika Itō as San.

Yukimitsu Ina (animation director for Tatami Time Machine Blues ) directed the anime, and kensuke ushio ( A Silent Voice , Chainsaw Man , DAN DA DAN ) composed the music. Hitomi Tateno , a veteran Studio Ghibli animator, was the animation producer, with the studio Sasayuri producing the anime.

The manga is set in a tropical southern island, and centers on San and her best friend Mayu, who go to the island's top all-girls school. War soon comes to their country, and the students of the school soon become embroiled in the war effort, and soon enough, the rear-line care of the wounded. One by one, San and Mayu lose their friends in the ever-worsening war.

Kyō released the manga in 2010, 65 years after the end of World War II. The anime's 2025 release came 80 years after the end of World War II.

Viz Media licensed the manga.

Kyō published the Mitsuami no Kami-sama manga in Shueisha 's now- defunct Jump X ( Jump Kai ) magazine in 2013, and Shueisha published the manga's first and only compiled book volume in the same year. The manga won an award in the 18th Annual Osamu Tezuka Cultural Prize in March 2014. The manga inspired Production I.G 's Pigtails 28-minute short anime film. The short made its international debut in April 2016 at the WorldFest Houston International Film Festival, where it won the Platinum Remi Award in the Classic Cel Animation Category. Pigtails has won multiple awards, including the Diamond Award in the Animated Film category at the 2016 California Film Awards.

title: Bleach Mirrors High Mobile Game's Opening Animation Trailer Reveals Theme Song, October 28 Launch
content:
The official website for Bandai Namco Entertainment 's Bleach Mirrors High mobile game announced on Tuesday that the game will launch on Wednesday for iOS and Android devices. The website streamed a video for the opening animation by the Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War anime's Studio Pierrot Films, and it reveals the theme song "CRITICAL" by suisoh :

New characters for the game designed by original creator Tite Kubo include:

Set in the wake of the Thousand-Year Blood War, “BLEACH Mirrors High” follows a lone soul newly awakened in Karakura Town as they take up the blade and carve an original Soul Reaper story all their own. Customize your Soul Reaper avatar's hair, face, body, eyes and more across a full color palette, then forge your ideal Zanpakuto, fine-tuning the blade, guard, hilt, decoration and effects. In battle, form a team of three and chain together fast, card-based attacks, signature special moves and the powerful “Soul Drive” team-up technique to trigger stylish Link Attacks. Fight alongside iconic characters such as Ichigo Kurosaki, Rukia Kuchiki and all-new Soul Reapers designed by series creator Tite Kubo .

Yū Sasahara is voicing Maiko Tokishima in the game, Shōgo Batori is voicing Giro Hando, and Fūka Izumi is voicing Naru Jurinna.

The game had a closed beta test that ran from July 22-29.

Bleach : Rebirth of Souls , the new 3D arena fighting game for the Bleach franchise , launched in March 2025.

KLab 's Bleach Soul Puzzle game launched for iOS and Android in September 2024, and ended service on April 14.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity , the fourth and final part of the Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War anime, debuted on July 25. Viz Media and Fathom Entertainment screened in advance the anime's first three episodes in U.S. theaters on June 25-29. The anime ended on Monday after a delay for the last two episodes.

title: Jujutsu Kaisen Returns With New Trailer for Major Event Ahead of Season 4
content:
Jujutsu Kaisen has returned for a new spoiler filled trailer hyping up its new exhibition coming to Japan while fans wait on the anime’s comeback for Season 4. Gege Akutami’s original Jujutsu Kaisen ended its manga run with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in 2024 , and to celebrate has announced it’s going to be hosting a special exhibition showing a close look at Akutami’s art and behind the scenes looks at how some of the biggest moments from the manga made it to the final page.

“Jujutsu Kaisen Final Exhibition” is a special event coming to Japan later this December, and will actually be hosted in Shinjuku, the sight of the final Shinjuku Showdown Arc for the series. With this new exhibition making its way to the region soon, Shueisha has dropped a slick trailer showing off some of the manga’s biggest moments from its final arc compared to the way Akutami had initially drafted them. You can check it out below, but beware there are some major spoilers here for those only caught up with the anime.

When Does Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 Come Out?

As for the anime itself, Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4: The Culling Game Part 2 is now in the works. A release window, date or international release platforms have yet to be announced as of this time, but it’s been revealed that Takeru Sato will be taking over as director for the new season after serving as an assistant director with Season 3. The rest of the production staff, voice cast, and more have also yet to be revealed. But it’s likely we’ll see more concrete updates on the anime soon enough following this exhibition.

Jujutsu Kaisen has been confirmed to be one of the many franchises that Shueisha will be showcasing during Jump Festa 2027 later this December , and the annual event is usually where the Shonen Jump titles reveal major updates about their in the works anime or manga productions. But with both Jujutsu Kaisen and the Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo sequel all completely over, this leaves a ton of room for a new update on the anime that could help tease what’s next to come for the franchise.

What to Know for Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4

It’s going to be one fight after another for Jujutsu Kaisen Season 4 too as it’s picking up right from where it all left off at the end of the third season. The anime ended with a massive cliffhanger with setting up the next major phase of Kenjaku’s Culling Game tournament, and there are many key fights that have yet to make their way to the anime. With a ton of new fighters, abilities, and more to see in action, it’s likely going to be as explosive of a season as the first three.

Serving as the penultimate arc of Jujutsu Kaisen overall, this next phase of the Culling Game has a lot of twists and turns that fans of the anime might not be ready for. Sukuna’s also been plotting something this entire time , and it seems like his grand plan is going into motion with the coming episodes too. But how are you liking the state of the Jujutsu Kaisen franchise right now? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Shonen Jump’s Next Cool Anime Hit Reveals First Look Ahead of 2027 Release
content:
Shonen Jump has a cool new anime coming our way next year, and now the series has dropped the first look and details for its production ahead of its launch. Four years after it first made its debut with Shueisha’s Jump SQ magazine , Neoshoco’s Phantom Busters has announced that it’s going to be making the jump to the TV screen next. It’s a series that has been building a lot of heat with fans thus far, but it’s likely going to find a whole new audience when the anime starts its takeover.

Phantom Busters previously announced that it would be coming to screens in 2027 with the debut of its new anime adaptation, but now the first official look at it has been revealed by TOHO Animation. Not only have they confirmed that they will be handling the animation production themselves with TOHO Animation STUDIO , but they have also revealed the four central cast members filling out the main group too. You can check out the first look at the Phantom Busters anime below.

When Does Phantom Busters Anime Come Out?

Phantom Busters is currently scheduled to make its debut sometime in 2027, but it has yet to confirm a more concrete release date or potential international release platforms as of the time of this writing. Chika Nagaoka will be directing the new anime for TOHO Animation STUDIO with Takahiro Kishida and Rina Iwamoto providing the character designs. There are still more members of the production staff being kept a mystery for now, but we’ll likely see more revealed during Jump Festa 2027 later this December .

The main voice cast for the Phantom Busters anime has been revealed, however, and they form the titular group itself with Nobuhiko Okamoto as Mogari Shishikuno, Natsuki Hanae as Eugene Korekishi, Koki Uchiyama as Kaoru Kanzaki, and Ryota Suzuki as Kotaro Tamon all confirmed thus far. It’s set to be one of the more curious new anime we’ll see debuting next year, and that makes 2027 all the more exciting thanks to how many franchises have been announced for a release thus far.

How to Check Out Phantom Busters

If you wanted to check out Phantom Busters yourself to better get ready for its anime debut next year, it’s actually now easier to do than ever before. Originally making its debut with Shueisha’s Jump SQ magazine in 2023, many of its back catalog chapters hadn’t been easily available outside of physical volume release. But seemingly as a way to tease the impeding anime announcement, Viz Media added Neoshoco’s entire series to their digital Shonen Jump library (with the three most recent chapters being available totally for free).

Phantom Busters is one of the many franchises that Shueisha will be showcasing during Jump Festa 2027 later this December, and that’s likely where we’ll get a much fuller update for the new anime series. With this first look now revealed, it seems like a perfect time to drop a teaser trailer or other updates. But how are you liking the look of Phantom Busters ‘ anime debut so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Witch on the Holy Night Film's Trailer Previews supercell's Theme Song
content:
Crunchyroll began streaming on Tuesday a trailer for the Witch on the Holy Night ( Mahōtsukai no Yoru ) anime film , and it previews the theme song "Yoru to Ao" (Night and Blue) by supercell .

The film will open in Japan on November 20. The original visual novel game's smartphone version will launch on the same day as the film's opening in Japan.

The film will feature returning cast:

• Haruka Tomatsu as Aoko Aozaki

• Kana Hanazawa as Alice Kuonji

• Yūsuke Kobayashi as Soujyuro Sizuki

The staff members are:

• Director: Masashi Takeuchi

• Character Design: Moe Tsuzuki

• Chief Animation Director: Masato Nagamori

• Script Production: ufotable

• Sub-Character Design: Nana Ishigo, Masato Nagamori

• Prop Design: Masato Saitō

• Compositing Director of Photography/Finishing Technical Director: Yuichi Terao

• 3D Director: Gōchū Satō

• Art Director: Koji Eto

• Color Key Artist: Mika Matsuoka

• Editing: Manabu Kamino

• Music: Hideyuki Fukasawa

• Chief Director: Hikaru Kondo

The story of the original Witch on the Holy Night visual novel is set in the late 1980s, and centers on protagonist Aoko Aozaki, one of two sister heirs to a long family line of modern mages. Although she is disinterested in magic, she is suddenly declared as the heir of their family's magical art, and reluctantly begins her apprenticeship under Alice Kuonji, a young witch who lives in a lonely manor atop a hill. Aoko balances her duties of learning the arcane, while also serving as her school's student council president. She also makes the acquaintance of Sōjūrō Shizuki (romanized as Soujyuro Sizuki in the English version of the game), a new transfer student who is unfamiliar with much of the modern world, and contends with the plots of her older sister Tōko Aozaki, who feels that her birthright has been denied.

Type-Moon most recently released the game on Steam in December 2023.

Aniplex released the PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch versions of the game in the West in December 2022, on the same day as the game's Japanese release date. The PS4 and Switch versions have sold more than 150,000 copies worldwide.

Mahōtsukai no Yoru was one of the first collaborations between Kinoko Nasu and artist Takashi Takeuchi in the mid-90s, preceding their founding of Type-Moon . Initially a novel, Nasu and Takeuchi only showed the draft to friends and did not officially release it. Type-Moon eventually developed it into a visual novel with graphics by Hirokazu Koyama that shipped in April 2012, with two sequels planned.

The story is noted for being one of the few tangible connections in the loosely connected "Nasuverse," the English-speaking fan term for the shared universe and cosmology in Type-Moon 's works, including Tsukihime , Fate/stay night , and The Garden of Sinners . An older Aoko Aozaki is an early mentor to Tsukihime protagonist Shiki Tohno, while an older Tōko Aozaki is an employer to Garden of Sinners protagonist Shiki Ryōgi. Tsukihime -A piece of blue glass moon-, the remake of Type-Moon 's Tsukihime dōjin visual novel game, launched in Japan for PS4 and Switch in August 2021. The game launched on PS4 and Switch in English in June 2024.

title: Bleach Creator Debuts New Soul Reapers With Surprising Anime Opening After Finale – Watch
content:
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has aired its final episode after 22 long years of the anime franchise, but the surprises are still coming as the franchise has returned with a new anime opening showing off a whole new roster of Soul Reapers designed by the original creator himself. Tite Kubo’s Bleach franchise has been in the midst of a massive comeback over the last few years with a new anime series adapting the long awaited final arc of the manga . And with that anime ending, fans thankfully still have much more to enjoy.

Bleach Mirrors High is officially going to be launching on mobile gaming platforms this week as part of the celebration for the anime’s grand finale, and it features a brand new story set right after the events of the Thousand-Year Blood War arc . This also introduces a whole new roster of Soul Reapers designed by series creator Tite Kubo, and they are on full display with the cool anime opening revealed for the game. You can check out the opening for Bleach Mirrors High in action below.

Bleach Mirrors High Introduces New Soul Reapers With Anime Opening

Bleach Mirrors High will be launching with iOS and Android on October 28th, and will see players utilizing their own character as they fight alongside notable fan favorites from the anime franchise. This new story is set in the wake of the Thousand-Year Blood War, and is notable because it’s a gap of time that’s never really been explored in the series itself. With the original events of the Bleach series skipping ahead ten years after Yhwach’s defeat for its finale, there’s an entire decade’s worth of time potentially to explore with what fans will see in the game’s story.

Previously revealed new characters include not only the two new central protagonists Shirin Migishima and and Shirane Sanari are Naru Jurinna as voiced by Fuka Izumi, Giro Hando as voiced by Shogo Batori, and Maiko Tokishima as voiced by Yu Sasahara . But this new trailer reveals the first look at even more of the extended roster all designed by Kubo himself. While no voice cast has been announced for the new characters, they are named as such:

• Hachirota Rohbe

• Tasuku Nimura

• Kuon Hoshimura

• Ibuki Kajimaru

• Mizuki Gandera

• Daikaku Sohaji

• Tamesu Gocho

• Kanuka Sanakura

• Seishiro Ginza

• Soyogi Sukenaga

What’s Next for Bleach ?

Bleach has now ended its official TV anime run with the release of its final episode after 22 years, but that doesn’t seem to be the end of new releases for the franchise overall. Not only is the franchise returning for this new mobile game pretty much immediately after the grand finale, but fans of the English dub can look forward to seeing the anime’s final two episodes themselves with Hulu later this November . There’s still even more coming down the pipeline too.

Ahead of the anime’s final episode, Bleach officially announced a new Bleach Fes. event taking place in Japan February 27-28 next year. This event will be bringing members of the production staff and voice cast together to celebrate the anime’s grand finale, but it would also be the perfect time to announce any potential continuation for the franchise. With Kubo already starting a sequel story, there’s a highly likely chance this anime is far from over too. But how are you liking this new squad of Soul Reapers so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

And with that anime ending, fans thankfully still have much more to enjoy.

Bleach Mirrors High is officially going to be launching on mobile gaming platforms this week as part of the celebration for the anime’s grand finale, and it features a brand new story set right after the events of the Thousand-Year Blood War arc . This also introduces a whole new roster of Soul Reapers designed by series creator Tite Kubo, and they are on full display with the cool anime opening revealed for the game. You can check out the opening for Bleach Mirrors High in action below.
Bleach Mirrors High Introduces New Soul Reapers With Anime Opening

Bleach Mirrors High will be launching with iOS and Android on October 28th, and will see players utilizing their own character as they fight alongside notable fan favorites from the anime franchise. This new story is set in the wake of the Thousand-Year Blood War, and is notable because it’s a gap of time that’s never really been explored in the series itself. With the original events of the Bleach series skipping ahead ten years after Yhwach’s defeat for its finale, there’s an entire decade’s worth of time potentially to explore with what fans will see in the game’s story.

Previously revealed new characters include not only the two new central protagonists Shirin Migishima and and Shirane Sanari are Naru Jurinna as voiced by Fuka Izumi, Giro Hando as voiced by Shogo Batori, and Maiko Tokishima as voiced by Yu Sasahara . But this new trailer reveals the first look at even more of the extended roster all designed by Kubo himself. While no voice cast has been announced for the new characters, they are named as such:
Hachirota Rohbe
Tasuku Nimura
Kuon Hoshimura
Ibuki Kajimaru
Mizuki Gandera
Daikaku Sohaji
Tamesu Gocho
Kanuka Sanakura
Seishiro Ginza
Soyogi Sukenaga
What’s Next for Bleach ?

contentBlocks.text: Bleach has now ended its official TV anime run with the release of its final episode after 22 years, but that doesn’t seem to be the end of new releases for the franchise overall. Not only is the franchise returning for this new mobile game pretty much immediately after the grand finale, but fans of the English dub can look forward to seeing the anime’s final two episodes themselves with Hulu later this November . There’s still even more coming down the pipeline too.

Ahead of the anime’s final episode, Bleach officially announced a new Bleach Fes. event taking place in Japan February 27-28 next year. This event will be bringing members of the production staff and voice cast together to celebrate the anime’s grand finale, but it would also be the perfect time to announce any potential continuation for the franchise. With Kubo already starting a sequel story, there’s a highly likely chance this anime is far from over too. But how are you liking this new squad of Soul Reapers so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Phantom Busters TV Anime Reveals Main Cast, Staff
content:
The official website for the television anime of Neoshoco 's Phantom Busters manga revealed the anime's teaser visual, main cast, and main staff members on Monday.

The anime will star:

• Nobuhiko Okamoto as Mogari Shishikuno

• Natsuki Hanae as Eugene Korekishi

• Kōki Uchiyama as Kaoru Kanzaki

• Ryōta Suzuki as Kōtarō Tamon

Chika Nagaoka ( Tamon’s B-Side , Uta no Prince Sama Maji Love Kingdom , Case Closed: The Fist of Blue Sapphire ) is directing the anime at TOHO animation STUDIO . Takahiro Kishida ( Haikyu!! , Durarara!! , Puella Magi Madoka Magica ) and Rina Iwamoto ( Blade & Bastard , Magical Suite Prism Nana ) are designing the characters.

The anime will air in 2027.

Viz Media releases the manga in English and describes the story:

Why bother fighting spectral foes like all the other exorcists when you can just eat them?

Straight A student Eugene Korekishi doesn't believe in ghosts…but his classmate Mogari Shishikuno is an exorcist who swallows them whole! Mogari can't see ghosts on his own, but once he and Eugene meet someone with the sight, there's only one path left—form an exorcist club at school and embark on a high school life that's anything but normal!

In search of a fourth member for the club, Mogari, Eugene, and new recruit Kaoru Kanzaki set their sights on Kotaro Tamon, a classmate who seems to be able to talk to ghosts. Unfortunately, Kotaro's got some major problems communicating with living humans! Will Kotaro be able to overcome his anxiety and join the Phantom Busters ?

Neoshoco launched the manga in Jump SQ. in 2023. Shueisha published the eighth compiled book volume on October 2. Viz Media released the fifth volume on October 6.

Viz Media 's Shonen Jump app and Shueisha 's MANGA Plus service are both releasing the manga digitally in English.

The manga has more than 1.4 million copies in circulation, including digital copies sold.

title: Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition TV Anime Reveals January 4 Debut, Returning Cast Members
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition ( Mairimashita! Iruma-kun if Episode of Mafia ), hiroja 's spinoff manga from Osamu Nishi 's Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun series, opened on Tuesday and revealed the anime's main visual, 12-episode run, and January 4 debut on NHK General at 11:00 p.m. JST.

The website also revealed the character visuals for returning cast members from the original Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun anime:

Ayumu Murase as Iruma

Mitsuki Saiga as Opera

Daisuke Ono as Naberius Callego

Ryōhei Kimura as Asmodeus Alice

Ayaka Asai as Valac Clara

Saori Hayami as Amelie

Get ready to meet the lovable cast of Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun as you've never seen them before! In this brand-new spinoff of the runaway hit series, Iruma is a dirt-poor but unfailingly cheerful young boy who grows up in a ruthless city slum. One day, Iruma gives an injured old man his last loaf of bread and nurses the stranger back to health—only to find out that the elder gent is none other than Don Sullivan, head of the Babyl Mafia! Soon after, Don Sullivan comes back, whisks Iruma away, and begs the boy to become his grandson. And just like that, Iruma begins his new life as the next in line to lead a gigantic gang of—dare we say—demonic mafiosos!

The spinoff manga launched in Akita Shoten 's Bessatsu Shōnen Champion magazine in September 2023. The manga moved to Akita Shoten 's Weekly Shōnen Champion magazine in December 2025. Akita Shoten published the manga's ninth compiled book volume on October 7.

Nishi's Kalego spinoff manga Mairimashita! Iruma-kun : Kalego Gaiden (Kalego Side Story) ended in January 2024. The series launched in Weekly Shōnen Champion in December 2023.

Nishi had written a previous two-chapter Kalego Gaiden spinoff manga in 2020.

Atsu Tsudanuma 's spinoff series Makai no Shuyaku wa Wareware da! (The Protagonist of the Demon World is Us) spinoff series was canceled and its final chapter was published in March 2025. The series is connected to the main Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun series, and is also a collaborative series with the "◯◯ no Shuyaku wa Wareware da" YouTuber group. The manga launched in Weekly Shōnen Champion in January 2020. Akita Shoten published the manga's 22nd and final volume in June 2025.

Nishi launched the Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun manga in Weekly Shōnen Champion in March 2017. The manga's first anime adaptation premiered in October 2019, and the second season premiered in April 2021, followed by the third season which debuted in October 2022. The fourth anime season debuted on April 4.

title: Shaman King's Hiroyuki Takei Designs Short Net Anime Mecha Samurai
content:
TV Tokyo announced on Monday that it is collaborating with the short net anime production company Plott to produce Mecha Samurai , a new short anime that will stream on YouTube and other online services starting in November. Shaman King creator Hiroyuki Takei drafted the anime's original main character designs. The anime's website also opened on Monday and started streaming a teaser video, and announced the anime's cast members.

The anime's "unorthodox samurai action" story is set in present-day Japan, where "Yōkai" (the Japanese term consists of the kanji for "ghost" and "machine"), or mechanical ghosts that appear from the "Demon Gate" from another dimension, have begun to attack and threaten humans. A young man named Chiaki Kuzumi, who fights as a samurai, battles the "Yōkai" with a katana imbued with the very power of the mechanical ghosts.

The anime will star:

Kentarō Mashiro as Chiaki Kuzumi, a young man chosen by the legendary katana "Benitora" as its wielder.

Riona Yamashita as Sana Fujimiya, a high-energy gamer girl from the prestigious Fujimiya family, who wields the "Tsukutsuku Denden" katana. Sana's katana gives her the ability to command "Tsukumogami," the spirit that dwells in household appliances.

Ayumu Mizukami as Kiyoharu Obana, a die hard money grubber who will not work for free. He wields the gun-shaped katana "Murakumo."

Ayumu Mizukami as Kaoru Rindō, a special instructor who teaches Chiaki and the others at a samurai training institute

Masaaki Mizunaka will also voice a character in the anime.

The creative studio TO2KYO2 is handling the graphic designs.

The anime will start streaming vertical shorts on November 2 on its YouTube , X (formerly Twitter ), Instagram, and TikTok accounts. The first pre-season episode will stream on YouTube on November 20, and the main series will stream in spring next year. This is TV Tokyo 's first anime production that is based on streaming and social media distribution.

Plott is known for producing web anime shorts such as the adaptation of Torinosasami. 's Teikō Penguin manga, and Konketsu no Karekore ( Karekore of Mixed Blood ), the adaptation of Momota Inoue 's Karekore manga. Plott recently launched on YouTube a new short anime titled Rakuraku Hanten on September 18. Plott also l aunched the first episode of Tengu Tōsen (Tengu Demon Sword Fight), a short anime project it is producing with Bandai Namco Entertainment , on YouTube on July 24.

The company previously produced the Anti-Hero Generations short anime adaptation based on Keita Uehara 's " Anti-Hero Generations " manga submission in 2022, which won the company's first "New Generation YouTube Manga Award" in 2021.

Plott recently announced its plan to produce over-the-air television anime next year, starting with three short anime series.

The company garners over 900 million monthly views across all its channels on YouTube , has over 14 million total subscribers, and its total number of views has exceeded 24 billion.

title: Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition Anime Main Visual and January 4 Revealed
content:
The spin-off anime Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition revealed the main visual, along with a January 4, 2027 premiere. The series will run for 12 episodes, with six character visuals also revealed. The franchise also has its first theatrical anime film project in development. For the spin-off anime, the returning cast includes:

• Ayumu Murase as Iruma

• Mitsuki Saiga as Opera

• Daisuke Ono as Naberius Kalego

• Ryohei Kimura as Asmodeus Alice

• Ayaka Asai as Valac Clara

• Saori Hayami as Ameri

You can also see the main visual below.

The Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun anime is based on Osamu Nishi’s manga serialized in Weekly Shonen Champion , which has 50 volumes published as of September 8, 2026. The anime premiered in 2019. Crunchyroll is streaming the anime, describing the story: Suzuki Iruma, human, 14, one day finds himself taken against his will into the world of demons. To add to his predicament, his doting owner and self-appointed “Grandpa” is the chair-demon at his new school. In order to survive, Iruma must deal with a haughty student who challenges him to a duel, a girl with adjustment issues, and so many more scary beings! Can this ultimate pacifist dodge the slings and arrows that are flung his way? As he struggles frantically, Iruma’s innate kindness begins to win over enemies.
